To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SCF induces a potent angiogenetic response in vivo and is overexpressed in primary human malignant gliomas and in glioma cell-infiltrated brain tissue.
SCF induces a potent angiogenesis within the CNS and that the SCF/cKit pathway plays an essential role in brain tumor- and normal brain cell-induced angiogenesis.
stem cell factor (SC) is expressed by glioma cells and neurons, and that SC induces angiogenesis in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the SCF/c-kit receptor pathway in gliomagenensis.
understanding how gliomas induce angiogenesis and how this process can be targeted for therapeutic purposes.
the mechanisms of angiogenesis in the brain and how this process contributes to the development of brain tumors, specifically glioma, the most common and most aggressive type of primary brain tumor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SCF/c- Kit signaling plays an important role during brain development and angiogenesis, and that it is up-regulated in brain tumors, where it contributes to gliomagenesis and tumor progression.

1) SCF is expressed by neurons, astrocytes and glioma cells, but not ECs; 2) glioma cells induce normal neurons to up-regulate SCF expression; 3) glioma cells express SCF in grade-dependent fashion; 4) SCF induces ECs to express c-Kit and to undergo morphological and functional changes in vitro; 5) SCF induces angiogenesis in vivo; 6) SCF induces tumor growth in vivo
the SCF/c-kit pathway plays an important and significant role in glioma growth and progression, and that it may be an important therapeutic target in the treatment of gliomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SCF is an important mediator of angiogenesis in the brain, both during normal development and in the context of glioma formation.
glioma cells and neurons overexpress SCF and that SCF is an autocrine/paracrine mediator that induces angiogenesis and gliomagenesis.
SCF is a novel angiogenic factor in the brain that is upregulated in glioma cells and neurons following injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SCF, a growth factor that is overexpressed in the brain after injury and by glioma cells and normal neurons in glioma-infiltrated regions, is an important regulator of glioma angiogenesis and gliomagenesis.
the c-Kit/SCF pathway plays an important proangiogenic role in brain tumor growth.
gliomas express stem cell factor (SC) in a grade-dependent pattern and that this SC is responsible for the glioma-mediated angiogenesis.
